gravity.source: WGS84 normal gravity (Somigliana formula, NIMA TR8350.2, 2000) with the TR8350.2 height series, at the two worst cases: the highest town (La Rinconada, Peru, up to 5,100 m, "the highest permanent settlement in the world", Wikipedia "La Rinconada, Peru", read 2026-10-11) put at the equator gives 9.7646; the lowest land (the Dead Sea shore, about 440 m below sea level in 2025 and falling about 1.1 m a year, Wikipedia "Dead Sea", read 2026-10-11) put at a pole gives 9.8335. Rounded outward to two decimals; the 0.006 margin above is about 2 km of further depth. The WGS84 constants, the height series and its constant m were checked against the ahrs 0.4.0 source code (MIT, PyPI: ahrs/common/constants.py, ahrs/utils/wgs84.py), which is what the cited page is built from. Weaknesses: TR8350.2 itself was not opened; every other web page named in the working was read only as a search excerpt. Working in research/34-planet-ranges.md.

airDensity.source: Dry air, ideal gas, ISO 2533 standard atmosphere. Densest: the record sea-level pressure 1083.8 hPa (Agata, Siberia, 31 December 1968, Wikipedia "Atmospheric pressure", read 2026-10-11) with the record low-station cold -67.8 °C (Verkhoyansk, 127 m, 1885 and 1892, Wikipedia "Verkhoyansk", read 2026-10-11) gives 1.8386. Thinnest: standard pressure at the highest town (5,100 m, 53,331 Pa at its geopotential height) with the hottest temperature ever recorded, 56.7 °C (Furnace Creek, 10 July 1913, disputed but accepted by the WMO, Wikipedia "Highest temperature recorded on Earth", read 2026-10-11) gives 0.5633. Rounded outward to two decimals. The ISA pressures were checked against ambiance 1.3.1 (Apache-2.0, PyPI). Weaknesses: each end joins extremes that never happen together, so the range is wide on purpose; dry air; the WMO archive itself and every other web page named in the working were read only as search excerpts; how far real pressure at 5,100 m falls below standard was not found. Working in research/34-planet-ranges.md.
